editorial:
You wake up to the same deadly day again and again, and Roy Pulver has to figure out why. Frank Grillo plays a tough former special forces guy who keeps getting killed in wild ways, then starts over. The movie mixes action, sci-fi, and dark humor, so it feels like a video game with real stakes. You follow him as he learns patterns, dodges assassins, and tries to protect his family. It is loud, fast, and easy to follow, with a fun energy that keeps you watching.

The action scenes are creative and the pacing rarely slows down. Grillo carries the movie well, and the supporting cast adds personality. Some jokes miss, and the story can feel thin between fights, but the loop idea stays entertaining. If you want a brain-off action night, this is a good pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Roy reaches Ventor, fights through his guards, and kills him. He then destroys the time machine that keeps resetting the day. The loop finally ends, and Roy gets a chance to move forward with his son and leave the deadly routine behind. After many failed attempts, he finally breaks the cycle and survives. The ending gives him closure and a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action movies with a time-loop twist.
